Zuma: The Outdoor Prisoner

By: Marion Edmunds | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Tonight we explore we explore South Africa's growing rapprochment with Russia and Putin's Africa plan

Unique Selling Point:
Building a clear story amongst the confusion around Zuma's attempts to dodge prison, his friendship with Russia and how it may be used to undermine his enemies.

Summary:
The dance continues.

As friends of Ukraine protest against a St Petersburg Ballet Performance outside Artscape and in Johannesburg, the contested relationship between South Africa and Vladimir Putin’s Russia is taking more twists and turns. This small cultural boycott shines a spotlight on an opaque relationship which is taking shape publically through political scandals and court judgements. And centre-stage is the former President Jacob Zuma who is currently in Russia, seeking medical treatment.

Last week, the Constitutional Court handed down a judgement which appeared to constitute a full stop in the long and winding process embarked on by former President Jacob Zuma to avoid jail for contempt for court, for failing to appear at the Zondo commission into State Capture. It stated that the decision by his once favoured spy boss, Arthur Fraser, in his capacity as Correctional Services Commissioner, to release him on medical parole in 2021 was unlawful.

This judgement – which might have been the final word on the long running saga – has not ironically finalised anything. In fact, it appears to have sparked a new game of cat and mouse between Zuma, his legal advisors, his friends in Russia and the forces of law and order in South Africa. And most of the action is happening behind closed doors, with no public scrutiny.

To recap: Jacob Zuma was sentenced to 15 months imprisonment after he failed to appear before the Zondo Commission into State Capture. His arrest sparked uncontrolled looting in Kwazulu-Natal and Johannesburg in which 300 people died and immense damage done to property, the economy and the confidence of the nation. However, he was released on medical parole after serving a fraction of his sentence, after Arthur Fraser over-ruled the Medical Parole Board to take a decision which has been repeatedly challenged in political rhetoric and through the courts. And while the controversy has rumbled on in the background, Zuma was deemed to have finished his sentence in October last year, despite the lawfulness of his medical parole being disputed.

The Constitutional Court Judgement now opens up the question as to whether he should return to jail to sit out the rest of the fifteen month sentence, or just part of it, or any of it at all. The Court has placed that decision on the shoulders of the Correctional Services Commissioner, who was appointed after this decision was made. He is currently mulling over the judgement.

However, in a sly move, the “outdoor prisoner” has gapped it to Russia for medical treatment. Sources close to him say this was deliberate and pre-emptive move, and would be a way too of upping the pressure on Ramaphosa who is preparing for the BRICS summit in August. Ramaphosa’s dilemma is that according to the ICC he would have to arrest Russia Premier, Vladimir Putin, for human rights violations should he come to South Africa, and the government has been actively trying to discourage him from coming here. According to our source, Zuma is now trying to meet Putin in Russia, and encourage him to attend the BRICS summit so that Ramaphosa is set up in a difficult situation.

At the same time, the information war around Russia and its engagement in Africa continues to rage. While Western-aligned analysts would see the country as a colonial power, extracting value from Africa in order to support continental political oligarchies, pro-Russian sympathisers believe that Russia is misrepresented and is in fact a re-incarnation of sorts of the Soviet friend it was to liberation movements, a sort of Cold War cos-play with 21st century weapons and real-politick.

Which brings us back to who defines South Africa’s relationship with Russia and what that means. A powerful faction in the ANC, aligned to Zuma, appear to be pushing for a pro-Russia policy, under the guise of a non-aligned stance, in order to soak up the solidarity and possible business opportunities that may provide. An anti-Russia faction – mainly opposition parties, civic organisations concerned with corruption, business leaders and pro-Ukraine movements are articulating the other perspective – that Russia is an undemocratic oppressive power at home and abroad. Aligning with Russia now would jeopardise South Africa’s future, in terms of the economy, and erode our democratic institutions further. Both sides are using the courts to make their point, but the dispute appears to be never-ending.

Press Release:


Dancing with Putin
South Africa’s friendship with Russia is a political football that finally came to a head on Wednesday. The Presidency put paid to all speculation that Russian President Vladmir Putin would attend the much anticipated BRICS summit to be held in Johannesburg, next month. The BRICS summit, which includes Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, would have seen Putin invited to attend this gathering of emerging market economies – a complication for President Cyril Ramaphosa who according to the International Criminal Court would have had to arrest Putin for human rights violations. The ICC issued arrest warrants for Putin for war crimes linked to the killing of women and children in Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. Meanwhile, the information war around Russia and its engagement in Africa continues to rage. While Western-aligned analysts would see the country as a colonial power, extracting value from Africa in order to support continental political oligarchies, pro-Russian sympathisers believe that Russia is misrepresented and is in fact a re-incarnation of sorts of the Soviet friend it was to liberation movements, a sort of Cold War cos-play with 21st century weapons and real-politick.
Producer: Marion Edmunds | Presenter: Govan Whittles

Script:


ZUMA: The Outdoor Prisoner - FINAL

IN CAPE TOWN, A SMALL GROUP PROTESTS AGAINST A BALLET, THEY CLAIM IS STAGED BY A TOURING COMPANY ASSOCIATED WITH RUSSIA.

THE UKRAINE ASSOCIATION IS LOBBYING SOUTH AFRICANS TO SEE RUSSIA’S INVASION OF UKRAINE FROM THEIR PERSPECTIVE.
THEY WANT A CULTURAL BOYCOTT.

DZVINKA KACHUR
President: Ukraine Association of South Africa
If all people here use their voices to stand against the violence to say, stand against oppression, this war would stop…there is a connection between supporting Russian culture and killing Ukrainian civilians.

SOUTH AFRICA’S STATED POLICY OF NON-ALIGNMENT IN THE UKRAINIAN CONFLICT HAS BEEN TESTED BY A SERIES OF EVENTS WHICH HAS SPLIT OPINION.

ON THE ONE SIDE THERE ARE THOSE WHO ACTIVELY SUPPORT VLADIMIR PUTIN’S RUSSIA - THIS INCLUDES SOUTH AFRICA’S FORMER PRESIDENT JACOB ZUMA. MZWANELE MANYI IS THE CONTROVERSIAL SPOKESPERSON FOR THE ZUMA FOUNDATION

MZWANELE MANYI
Spokesperson: Jacob Zuma Foundation
The connection between South Africa and Soviet, now Russia, continues to be strong …When South Africa needed help … they also gave them guns so that they're able to fight the struggle. So yeah, indeed, the the connection is very deep.

ZUMA’s RELATIONSHIP WITH PUTIN IS ALSO PERSONAL.
IN THIS VIDEO, ZUMA REMINISCES ABOUT HOW PUTIN SAVED HIM FROM AN AWFUL DEATH.

JACOB ZUMA in video:
I knew that my friend who was at that time was the President of his country would be the only one in the country that will assist me,. He sent doctors ….there were three different types of poison that were put to me, together.

FOR INVESTIGATIVE LEGAL JOURNALIST KARYN MAUGHAN, THIS FIRST-HAND ACCOUNT IS A USEFUL WAY TO UNDERSTAND SOUTH AFRICA’S APPROACH TO RUSSIA UNDER ZUMA’S PRESIDENCY.

KARYN MAUGHAN
Senior legal journalist and author: News24
The fact that Jacob Zuma received the so-called life-saving treatment - literally within days of South Africa signing that unlawful nuclear deal with Rosatom, the Russian nuclear agency, speaks to the kind of powerful hold I would argue Putin has on him.

KARYN HAS WRITTEN A BOOK ABOUT THE FAILED NUCLEAR DEAL.
IT EXPOSES ONE OF THE ROLES THAT RUSSIA WOULD LIKE TO PLAY IN SOUTH AFRICA, AS A SUPPLIER OF NUCLEAR TECHNOLOGY.

GOVAN WHITTLES:... do you think that Zuma is trying to extend Russia's influence in South Africa?

KARYN MAUGHAN: Absolutely. What I find so frightening within that book was to see how Kremlin intelligence had infiltrated the South African environment.

ZUMA’S LEGAL CHALLENGES ARE SQUARELY ON KARYN’S REPORTING BEAT - INCLUDING HIS PERFORMANCE AT THE ZONDO COMMISSION ON STATE CAPTURE, SET UP TO PROBE THE ROT IN THE SOUTH AFRICAN ESTABLISHMENT.

GOVAN WHITTLES PTC: In July 2021, the Constitutional Court sentenced former President Jacob Zuma to 15 months behind bars for walking out and defying the Zondo commission. Two months later, he was controversially released on medical parole. That decision was contested from Day One. And two years later, we're back here, where the Constitutional Court has confirmed the decision to release him on medical parole was unlawful

BUT MANYI SAYS THERE IS NO NEED FOR JACOB ZUMA TO GO BACK TO PRISON - THE SENTENCE WAS SERVED ON THE OTHER SIDE OF THE BARS, WHILE HE WAS ON PAROLE.

MZWANELE MANYI
Spokesperson: Jacob Zuma Foundation
What that Constitutional Court did was a very hateful sentence that they give to President Zuma. Be that as it may, he respected the law, he handed himself over and he served his time.

ZUMA’s CRITICS SAY HE MUST GO BACK TO JAIL.

IN THE MEANTIME, THE OUTDOOR PRISONER IS A STEP AHEAD.

PTC GOVAN WHITTLES: Before the prospect of the former president returning to jail even hit the Twitterverse, Jacob Zuma took off, hightailing it to Zimbabwe and then Russia.

ONCE AGAIN ZUMA HAS GONE TO RUSSIA FOR MEDICAL TREATMENT - OFFICIALLY HE WILL ONLY RETURN TO SOUTH AFRICA ONCE HE GETS THE GREEN LIGHT FROM RUSSIAN DOCTORS.

GOVAN WHITTLES: what is wrong with former President Jacob Zuma? Medically speaking?

MANYI: I'm not a doctor, I wouldn't be able to do that…even if I did know.It would not be my business to go around sharing his medical issues with the world.

GOVAN WHITTLES: Why does Mr. Zuma need to go for medical treatment in Russia?

MANYI: We don't trust that when President Zuma is in these facilities that he'll be safe. President Zuma's got too many enemies.

GOVAN WHITTLES: So you're saying that if former President Zuma was treated in the South African hospital, the people in the medical fraternity might try to kill?

MANYI: Yeah. Can't rule that out. Yes.

IN CONVERSATIONS WITH OTHER SOURCES, WE LEARNT THAT ZUMA MIGHT ALSO SEEK A MEETING WITH PUTIN.

MZWANELE MANYI: Yeah, so what's what's what's wrong with that? So President Zuma and President Putin go back a long way. …. the men have got a very long standing relationship.

SPEAKING FROM RUSSIA, A PRO-KREMLIN ANALYST, DR LEONID SAVIN, WAS ABLE TO FILL US IN FURTHER ABOUT THE SOUTH AFRICA - RUSSIA AXIS.

LEONID SAVIN
Geopolitical Analyst
Vladimir Putin comes from Soviet elite. And during Soviet time, Soviet Union assisted them much to African countries. There was idea of international … solidarity and Russia provided a lot of different types of food, the money, etc. And now Russia is back to this kind of agenda to support African countries. Soviet Union supported the struggle against Western powers, who have some colonialism in Africa.

GOVAN WHITTLES: To be fair, Dr Savin, Russia is accused of the very same thing, of propping up corrupt regimes on the African continent. … in what way is Russia not a colonial power?

LEONID SAVIN: Russia that cannot be neo-colonial power for African countries for for many reasons. Our strategic culture is different.

IN THE MEANTIME, PUTIN IS FACING A WARRANT OF ARREST BY THE INTERNATIONAL CRIMINAL COURT ISSUED FOR RUSSIA’S ABDUCTION OF UKRAINIAN CHILDREN.
ICC sound up about the warrant of the ICC: The International Criminal Court has issued a warrant of arrest for Vladimir Putin

THIS MEANS THAT ALL SIGNATORIES TO THE ICC WOULD HAVE TO ARREST PUTIN SHOULD HE VISIT THEIR COUNTRIES.
LEADERS OF THE FOUNDING BRICS MEMBER COUNTRIES: BRAZIL, RUSSIA, INDIA AND CHINA WERE SLATED TO ATTEND THE AUGUST BRICS SUMMIT IN GAUTENG IN PERSON, PUTTING THE SOUTH AFRICAN GOVERNMENT IN A DIFFICULT POSITION, GIVEN ITS STATED RELUCTANCE TO POUNCE ON PUTIN.

KARYN MAUGHAN
Senior legal journalist and author: News24
in the last two weeks, preceding this, the DA launching an application to have South Africa's obligations under the ICC recognised, ie that it will be forced to, to arrest Vladimir Putin if and when he arrived for the BRICS conference in August,

BEFORE THE APPLICATION EVEN GOT TO OPEN COURT, THE PAPERS WERE RELEASED PUBLICALLY. AMONG THEM WAS PRESIDENT RAMAPHOSA’S AFFIDAVIT IN WHICH HE MADE A STARTLING ARGUMENT.

GOVAN WHITTLES PTC:
It's an explosive claim … that an attempt to arrest Vladimir Putin in South Africa would be a declaration of war against Russia. This argument suggests that South Africa is motivated by fear and not principle.

THE COURT ENFORCED THE ICC RULING, OBLIGING THE SOUTH AFRICAN GOVERNMENT TO COMMIT UNEQUIVOCALLY TO SEIZING PUTIN SHOULD HE PUT FOOT ON SOUTH AFRICAN SOIL.
MEANWHILE, IN MAY THIS YEAR THE US AMBASSADOR ACCUSED SOUTH AFRICA OF SELLING WEAPONS ILLEGALLY TO RUSSIA, LOADING THEM SECRETLY ON TO THE SANCTIONED VESSEL, THE LADY R.
THERE IS NOW A CHANCE WE MAY LOSE A PREFERENTIAL TRADE DEAL WITH AMERICA CALLED AGOA, DOING HEAVY DAMAGE TO THE SOUTH AFRICAN ECONOMY.

MZWANELE MANYI
Spokesperson: Jacob Zuma Foundation
What would happen if you are going to arrest Putin? Do you want a AGOA? Or do you want peace? What is it that you want? We want peace.

AT THIS PRE-BRICS CONFERENCE IN GAUTENG LAST WEEK, THE MOOD WAS UPBEAT IN ANTICIPATION OF A SUMMIT WHICH SOME THINK MAY DISRUPT THE WORLD’S EXISTING POWER BALANCES, ACCORDING TO THE GENERAL SECRETARY OF THE SACP, SOLLY MAPAILA.

SOLLY MAPAILA
General Secretary: SACP
BRICS is an important platform in that it creates the possibility to towards a multipolar world system. It may actually even become more important in the long run than the United Nations,

GOVAN WHITTLES PTC:
As political parties met to prepare for the summit, President Ramaphosa announced that Putin isn’t coming.

THERE’S A SENSE OF RELIEF THAT RAMAPHOSA WAS ABLE TO NEGOTIATE THIS COMPROMISE TO ALLOW BRICS TO TAKE PLACE IN AUGUST WITHOUT INCIDENT. IN FACT, ANC SPOKESPERSON MAHLENGI BHENGU-MOTSIRI SEES IT AS A VICTORY.

MAHLENGI BHENGU-MOTSIRI
Spokesperson: ANC
I think it is a victory for statesmanship. But I don't think it is just about our president, I think it is about our continent. And I think it is about the global south.

KARYN MAUGAN
Senior legal journalist and author: News24
I think the people who really deserve the congratulations is the judiciary itself, and the people within that legal environment who ensure that we have legal precedents that categorically state that we are obliged to arrest him.

AS THE LIGHT FALLS OUTSIDE THE THEATRE, THE UKRAINE ASSOCIATION IS UPBEAT. IN THIS SIDE-DRAMA TO THEIR DREADFUL WAR, THEIR ARCH-ENEMY HAS BEEN KEPT AT BAY.




PROMOS:

ONE: A CULTURAL BOYCOTT ON SOUTH AFRICAN SOIL….
DZVINKA KACHUR
President: Ukraine Association of South Africa
This is what we are trying to communicate to ordinary South Africans, that there is a connection between supporting Russian culture and killing Ukrainian civilians
AND PUSH-BACK FROM THE POLITICIANS
SOLLY MAPAILA
General Secretary: SACP
The reality is that Putin has stood up to this bullies

TWO: DEALS, DIPLOMACY AND A NEW WORLD ORDER - HOW FAR DOES RUSSIAN INFLUENCE EXTEND IN SOUTH AFRICA?
KARYN MAUGHAN
Senior legal journalist and author: News24
What I find so frightening within that book was to see how Kremlin intelligence had infiltrated the South African environment.

THREE:)COLD WAR LOYALTIES IN A NEW WORLD ORDER
LEONID SAVIN
Geopolitical Analyst
Russia back to this kind of agenda to support African countries.
WHAT IS PUTIN’S AFRICA PLAN - AND HOW MUCH WILL IT COST?
MZWANELE MANYI
Spokesperson: Jacob Zuma Foundation
Do you want a AGOA? Or do you want peace? What is it that you want? We want peace.

Carte Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 10 August 2023 TX Date: 0000-00-00 Press Release: Dancing with Putin South Africa’s friendship with Russia is a political football that finally came to a head on Wednesday. The Presidency put paid to all speculation that Russian President Vladmir Putin would attend the much anticipated BRICS summit to be held in Johannesburg, next month. The BRICS summit, which includes Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, would have seen Putin invited to attend this gathering of emerging market economies – a complication for President Cyril Ramaphosa who according to the International Criminal Court would have had to arrest Putin for human rights violations. The ICC issued arrest warrants for Putin for war crimes linked to the killing of women and children in Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. Meanwhile, the information war around Russia and its engagement in Africa continues to rage. While Western-aligned analysts would see the country as a colonial power, extracting value from Africa in order to support continental political oligarchies, pro-Russian sympathisers believe that Russia is misrepresented and is in fact a re-incarnation of sorts of the Soviet friend it was to liberation movements, a sort of Cold War cos-play with 21st century weapons and real-politick. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Tonight we explore we explore South Africa's growing rapprochment with Russia and Putin's Africa plan
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Building a clear story amongst the confusion around Zuma's attempts to dodge prison, his friendship with Russia and how it may be used to undermine his enemies.
metadata.Summary: The dance continues. As friends of Ukraine protest against a St Petersburg Ballet Performance outside Artscape and in Johannesburg, the contested relationship between South Africa and Vladimir Putin’s Russia is taking more twists and turns. This small cultural boycott shines a spotlight on an opaque relationship which is taking shape publically through political scandals and court judgements. And centre-stage is the former President Jacob Zuma who is currently in Russia, seeking medical treatment. Last week, the Constitutional Court handed down a judgement which appeared to constitute a full stop in the long and winding process embarked on by former President Jacob Zuma to avoid jail for contempt for court, for failing to appear at the Zondo commission into State Capture. It stated that the decision by his once favoured spy boss, Arthur Fraser, in his capacity as Correctional Services Commissioner, to release him on medical parole in 2021 was unlawful. This judgement – which might have been the final word on the long running saga – has not ironically finalised anything. In fact, it appears to have sparked a new game of cat and mouse between Zuma, his legal advisors, his friends in Russia and the forces of law and order in South Africa. And most of the action is happening behind closed doors, with no public scrutiny. To recap: Jacob Zuma was sentenced to 15 months imprisonment after he failed to appear before the Zondo Commission into State Capture. His arrest sparked uncontrolled looting in Kwazulu-Natal and Johannesburg in which 300 people died and immense damage done to property, the economy and the confidence of the nation. However, he was released on medical parole after serving a fraction of his sentence, after Arthur Fraser over-ruled the Medical Parole Board to take a decision which has been repeatedly challenged in political rhetoric and through the courts. And while the controversy has rumbled on in the background, Zuma was deemed to have finished his sentence in October last year, despite the lawfulness of his medical parole being disputed. The Constitutional Court Judgement now opens up the question as to whether he should return to jail to sit out the rest of the fifteen month sentence, or just part of it, or any of it at all. The Court has placed that decision on the shoulders of the Correctional Services Commissioner, who was appointed after this decision was made. He is currently mulling over the judgement. However, in a sly move, the “outdoor prisoner” has gapped it to Russia for medical treatment. Sources close to him say this was deliberate and pre-emptive move, and would be a way too of upping the pressure on Ramaphosa who is preparing for the BRICS summit in August. Ramaphosa’s dilemma is that according to the ICC he would have to arrest Russia Premier, Vladimir Putin, for human rights violations should he come to South Africa, and the government has been actively trying to discourage him from coming here. According to our source, Zuma is now trying to meet Putin in Russia, and encourage him to attend the BRICS summit so that Ramaphosa is set up in a difficult situation. At the same time, the information war around Russia and its engagement in Africa continues to rage. While Western-aligned analysts would see the country as a colonial power, extracting value from Africa in order to support continental political oligarchies, pro-Russian sympathisers believe that Russia is misrepresented and is in fact a re-incarnation of sorts of the Soviet friend it was to liberation movements, a sort of Cold War cos-play with 21st century weapons and real-politick. Which brings us back to who defines South Africa’s relationship with Russia and what that means. A powerful faction in the ANC, aligned to Zuma, appear to be pushing for a pro-Russia policy, under the guise of a non-aligned stance, in order to soak up the solidarity and possible business opportunities that may provide. An anti-Russia faction – mainly opposition parties, civic organisations concerned with corruption, business leaders and pro-Ukraine movements are articulating the other perspective – that Russia is an undemocratic oppressive power at home and abroad. Aligning with Russia now would jeopardise South Africa’s future, in terms of the economy, and erode our democratic institutions further. Both sides are using the courts to make their point, but the dispute appears to be never-ending.
